tip.title: Take a 10-minute nap after a short night
tip.why: In a sleep-lab study, healthy adults restricted to five hours of sleep took naps of 0, 5, 10, 20 or 30 minutes. The 10-minute nap gave the best mix of benefits, with lower sleepiness and better performance within minutes that lasted about 2.5 hours. Longer naps left people groggy first. It was a small lab study, so treat it as a useful guide.
how: Set a timer for 10 minutes, ideally before 3 PM.
Lie down or recline somewhere dim and quiet; you do not have to fall fully asleep.
Get up when the timer ends and step into daylight.
tip.ask: What does research say about the best nap length after a short night's sleep, and who should avoid napping?

markets.headline: Stocks edged up for a third day on Wednesday after the Fed held rates, with the Nasdaq up 0.3% and Tesla down 0.8%; Alphabet fell after hours on a weaker quarter.
points: The S&P 500 closed at 7,743.98 (+0.3%), the Nasdaq at 26,549.85 (+0.3%) and the Dow at 52,475.10 (+0.2%) after the Fed left its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4%.
The Fed vote was 10 to 2, and both dissenters wanted a quarter-point increase; CME FedWatch put the odds of a December hike near 85%.
Tesla slipped 0.8% to $404.22 after a two-day rally tied to speculation about a SpaceX combination; Reuters reported no terms have been agreed.

After the close, Microsoft beat expectations and gained over 4% in extended trading, while Alphabet missed and fell more than 7%, renewing worries about AI spending. The Russell 2000 row still shows Monday's close because later closes could not be confirmed.

pick.name: Seagate Technology
pick.what: Seagate makes hard disk drives and storage systems, with large data-center customers that store the data behind cloud and AI services.
pick.why: It rose 2.2% on Oct 26 to $644.21 after falling roughly 30% over the past month, and the consensus of 26 analysts reads Strong Buy with an average target near $1,138. Barclays kept a Buy with a $1,250 target and Bank of America a Buy with $1,200 on Oct 21. An idea to research, not a recommendation.
pick.risk: The stock is still far below its 52-week high of $1,145, and a roughly 30% drop in a month shows how fast sentiment can turn. UBS rates it Hold, and demand depends on AI data-center spending holding up.

btc.summary: In his Oct 25 video, "Bitcoin: Bears Regaining Control," and in posts around it, Cowen said two straight weekly closes below the level he had been watching confirm that the September breakout was a fakeout, and that the rally has now been fully unwound. His next downside reference is the bull market support band, the zone formed by the 20-week average and 21-week exponential average. He ticked off two of nine steps on a bearish Q4 roadmap tied to the pattern of weakness late in US midterm years, and said the roadmap is void only if Bitcoin reclaims and holds that level. The next steps depend on the Fed decision and inflation data.

news.title: Nvidia and AMD to invest $4 billion in Meta as the AI partnership deepens

news.title: Anthropic's IPO leads a $235 billion day of AI dealmaking

news.ask: What does a single day of $235 billion in AI financing say about how the buildout is being paid for, and where is the fragility?

news.title: Unitree's quarterly revenue jumps 70% in its first report since listing
news.blurb: Third-quarter revenue rose 70% from a year earlier, though net profit fell. The report follows a demo video of its H2-X humanoid performing combat moves that helped drive a recent share rally.
news.ask: Revenue up 70% while profit fell: what does that say about the cost of scaling humanoid production, and how does it compare with US makers?

news.title: Alphabet misses estimates and AI spending worries return
news.blurb: Alphabet's quarterly results came in below expectations and its shares fell more than 7% after hours, while Microsoft beat and rose over 4%. The split put AI capital spending back in focus.
news.ask: Why did Microsoft's AI spending read as a strength while Alphabet's read as a worry, and what would change that view?

vocab.def: Too great or extraordinary to be put into words.
vocab.ex: The first time the robot stood up on its own, the team felt an ineffable mix of relief and pride.

cards.b: Latin ineffabilis, from in- 'not' + effari 'to speak out'
inexpressible, indescribable, unspeakable
feelings, beauty or experiences that words fall short of, usually in a good way

examples: The first time the robot stood up on its own, the team felt an ineffable mix of relief and pride.
There was something ineffable about the view from the ridge at sunset.

vocab.def: Quick to notice and understand things that others miss.
vocab.ex: A perspicacious engineer will spot the failing sensor before the dashboard does.

cards.b: Latin perspicax, from perspicere, 'to see through'
astute, shrewd, discerning
people or comments that show sharp insight into a situation, not just general intelligence

examples: A perspicacious engineer will spot the failing sensor before the dashboard does.
Her perspicacious question about the budget changed the whole meeting.

vocab.def: Lasting for a very short time.
vocab.ex: The fall color in the foothills is ephemeral; by mid-November most of it is gone.

cards.b: Greek ephemeros, 'lasting a day', from epi 'on' and hemera 'day'
fleeting, transient, short-lived
things that are expected to disappear quickly, like trends, moments, messages or blossoms

examples: The fall color in the foothills is ephemeral; by mid-November most of it is gone.
Some chat apps make messages ephemeral by deleting them after a day.

vocab.def: Using very few words; brief and to the point.
vocab.ex: Her laconic reply, 'Shipped,' told the team everything they needed to know.

cards.b: Greek Lakonikos, 'of Laconia', the region of Sparta, whose people were known for short, blunt speech
terse, succinct, concise
describing a person, a reply or a style of writing that says a lot in few words

examples: Her laconic reply, 'Shipped,' told the team everything they needed to know.
He was a laconic host, but nobody ever left his dinners hungry or confused.

vocab.def: Showing steady, careful and persistent effort.
vocab.ex: The sedulous engineer re-ran every calibration before the demo.

cards.b: Latin sedulus, diligent or attentive
diligent, assiduous, industrious
praising careful, patient work, like testing, editing or research

examples: The sedulous engineer re-ran every calibration before the demo.
Her sedulous note-taking meant nothing from the meeting was lost.

vocab.def: Friendly, lively and welcoming, especially of a gathering, a host or an atmosphere around food and drink.
vocab.ex: The reception had a convivial mood, with strangers swapping stories at every table.

cards.b: Latin convivium, a feast: con- (together) plus vivere (to live)
sociable, genial, festive
describing a party, a dinner, a host or the mood of a room

examples: The reception had a convivial mood, with strangers swapping stories at every table.
She is a convivial host who always makes sure everyone has a drink and someone to talk to.

vocab.def: Most noticeable or important; standing out from the rest.
vocab.ex: The salient point of the demo was that the hand worked without retraining.

cards.b: Latin salire, to leap: a salient fact leaps out at you
prominent, key, striking
naming the main point in a report, a meeting or a demo

examples: The salient point of the demo was that the hand worked without retraining.
Skip the background and lead with the three salient numbers.

spanish.pron: KOH-moh teh fweh en lah CHAM-bah
spanish.note: 'Chamba' is casual Mexican slang for work or a job. Use it with friends and coworkers, not in a formal email.

cards.en: I have work left to do

dialog.en: A bit heavy, but I'm done.

spanish.use: Ask it to a friend or coworker when they come home or log off for the day.

spanish.note: Literally 'I'm made into dust.' A common casual way to say you are exhausted. Women say 'hecha polvo.'
spanish.use: Say it after a short night or a long day, to a friend or coworker.

spanish.note: 'Bronca' means trouble or a problem in casual Mexican Spanish. Say it to wave off an apology or reassure someone; it is friendly and informal.

dialog.en: Thanks, I already have the coffee.

spanish.use: Say it when a friend apologizes for being late or asks if a small favor is okay.

spanish.note: 'Chido' is very common casual Mexican slang for cool or great. It is friendly and informal, fine with friends and peers.

dialog.en: Did you see my new car?
Yes! Your car is so cool!

spanish.use: Say it when a friend shows you something you like, like a car, a phone or a new place.

options: Where did you park your car?

spanish.phrase: Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos
spanish.pron: ah-oh-REE-tah VEN-goh, voy por OO-nohs TAH-kohs
spanish.meaning: I'll be right back, I'm getting some tacos.
spanish.note: 'Ahorita' is flexible in Mexico: it can mean right now or a while from now, depending on tone. 'Ahorita vengo' is the usual way to say you are stepping out and coming back soon.

cards.en: I'll be back in a bit

parts.en: in a little while / right now

dialog.es: Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos.
dialog.en: I'll be right back, I'm getting some tacos.
Can you bring me two al pastor?
Sure, I'll bring them in a bit.

spanish.use: Say it when you step out of a room or a shop for a few minutes and plan to come back.

options: I'll be right back, I'm getting some tacos.
I already ate all the tacos.

spanish.note: The standard cheer at a Mexican wedding toast, shouted by the whole room. 'Novios' means the bride and groom, or a couple who are engaged or newly married. It's for weddings and anniversaries.

dialog.en: And may they dance all night!
Exactly! Now, to the dance floor.

spanish.use: Say it when someone raises a glass at a wedding, or after a friend announces an engagement.

options: The bus leaves in five minutes.

spanish.phrase: Ni modo, ya será para la próxima
spanish.pron: nee MOH-doh, yah seh-RAH PAH-rah lah PROHK-see-mah
spanish.meaning: Oh well, there's always next time.
spanish.note: 'Ni modo' is the everyday Mexican shrug for something that can't be changed. Add 'ya será para la próxima' after a missed plan to move on lightly; it's not for serious losses.

dialog.es: Se canceló el partido por la lluvia.
dialog.en: The game was canceled because of the rain.

dialog.es: Ni modo, ya será para la próxima.
dialog.en: Oh well, there's always next time.
Want to go get tacos then?

spanish.use: Say it when a plan falls through and you'd rather move on than complain, like a missed flight or a canceled game.

options: Oh well, there's always next time.

phrases: Ni modo, ya será para la próxima
Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos
